kits.familyName: Following the rules the workplace must meet
setup: You work as {role|a} at {workplace|a}, where a compliance guide lists the rules every employee follows.
As {role|a} at {workplace|a}, you follow a compliance guide that spells out required rules for your work.
pressure: {coworker3} says nobody ever checks these rules.
You are in the middle of a busy afternoon.

tiers.1: An item that could hurt customers comes off the floor before anything else.
tiers.2: Work that needs a current certificate cannot go on without one.
tiers.3: A false or missing record misleads everyone who relies on it.
tiers.4: Requests for personal records follow a set route for a reason.
tiers.5: A missing required notice should be restored, but it can wait behind urgent problems.

fact: The compliance guide says recalled items come off the sales floor at once, and a recall notice just listed an item on your shelf.
issues.short: the recalled item on the shelf
issues.action: Pull the item from the shelf and tell {lead|the} right away.
issues.reason: A recall notice means the item may harm customers, so it comes off the floor before anything else.
issues.lesson: When a notice says an item is unsafe, remove it first and report it.

shortcut.text: Finish stocking the aisle first and pull the item at the end of your shift.
shortcut.why: Customers could buy the item while you finish, and the guide says to remove it at once.
shortcut.mis: Routine work should be finished before acting on a notice.

clear: {Lead|the} already pulled an item named in a recall notice and logged it.
issues.done: the recalled item is already off the shelf

fact: Your certificate to run {equipment|the} expired yesterday, and the compliance guide says only staff with a current certificate may run it.
issues.action: Stop running it and ask {lead|the} how to renew your certificate.
issues.brief: stop and ask to renew the certificate
issues.reason: The guide allows only staff with a current certificate, so recent training does not cover you until it is renewed.
issues.lesson: If a required certificate has expired, stop that task and get it renewed.

shortcut.text: Keep running it until the renewal paperwork arrives, since you were certified recently.
shortcut.why: An expired certificate means you are no longer cleared under the guide, however recently it ran out.
shortcut.mis: A certificate that expired recently still counts.

clear: Your certificate to run {equipment|the} was already renewed, and {lead|the} confirmed it is on file.

fact: You did yesterday's inspection but left the log blank, and the guide says each log is completed on the day of inspection.
issues.action: Complete the log with today's date and a note that it was filled in late.
issues.brief: log it today and note it was late
issues.reason: A late entry that says it is late keeps the record true. A backdated entry would be a false record.
issues.lesson: Complete required records honestly, even when late, and never backdate them.

shortcut.text: Fill in the log with yesterday's date so it looks complete.
shortcut.why: Backdating makes a false record, even when the inspection really happened.
shortcut.mis: A complete-looking log matters more than an honest one.

clear: The late inspection log was already completed with a note saying it was filled in late.
issues.done: the late log entry is already recorded

fact: A customer asks for a copy of everything recorded about them, and the compliance guide says these requests go to the privacy office.
issues.action: Tell the customer how to send the request to the privacy office.
issues.brief: point them to the privacy office
issues.reason: The guide sends these requests to people trained to decide what can be released.
issues.lesson: Send requests for personal records through the route the guide names.

shortcut.text: Print what you can find and hand it over so the customer is not kept waiting.
shortcut.brief: hand over what you can find
shortcut.why: You might release information the privacy office would have held back.
shortcut.mis: Helping quickly means handing over whatever you can find.

clear: The privacy office already has a customer's request for their records.
issues.done: the privacy office already has the request

fact: The compliance guide says the required notice in the break room must stay posted, and it has fallen off the wall.
issues.action: Put the notice back up and mention it to {lead|the}.
issues.brief: repost the notice and mention it
issues.reason: A required notice only helps if people can see it, and telling {lead|the} stops it from happening again.
issues.lesson: Keep required notices visible and report it when one comes down.

shortcut.text: Leave it on the table, since everyone already knows what it says.
shortcut.why: Not everyone has read it, and the guide says it must stay posted.
shortcut.mis: A rule everyone knows needs no notice.

proceed.text: Carry on with your regular work, since nothing here needs action.
proceed.why: Each of these situations involves a rule in the guide that applies to every employee.
proceed.lesson: The rules in a compliance guide apply to everyone who works there.

generic.text: Ask {coworker2} what they usually do and copy that.
generic.why: A coworker's habit is not the guide, and it may be out of date.
generic.mis: Common practice matches the written rules.

generic.text: Wait for someone to point out the problem before you act.
generic.why: The guide applies to you now, and waiting leaves the problem in place.
generic.mis: Rules only matter once someone notices.

overcaution.text: Stop all your work until {lead|the} reviews every rule in the guide with you.
overcaution.why: The problem is specific, and stopping everything delays work that is allowed.
overcaution.mis: Any rule question means stopping all work.

setup: A recall notice lists an item that is on the shelves where you work.

steps.text: Read the notice to match the item
Take the item off the shelf
Record what was removed and who you notified

rel: You need to be sure which item before you remove it.
Your report should say which item the notice means.
The record should include who was told.
process.lesson: Match the item, remove it, report it, then keep the record.

title: Compliance reminders
intro: You are checking a reminder sheet before it is posted in the break room.
prompt: Which line gives advice that breaks the guide?
doc.lesson: Reminder sheets must match what the compliance guide actually requires.

lines.text: Take recalled items off the sales floor at once and tell your lead.
lines.fine: Keeps unsafe items away from customers.

bad.text: Take recalled items off the sales floor at the end of your shift.
bad.why: Customers could buy the item in the meantime. The guide says to remove it at once.

lines.text: Stop work that needs a certificate once yours has expired.
lines.fine: Keeps work within what you are cleared to do.

bad.text: Keep doing work that needs a certificate for a week after it expires.
bad.why: The guide allows only staff with a current certificate, with no grace week.

lines.text: Complete each inspection log on the day of the inspection.
lines.fine: Keeps the record close to the event.

bad.text: If you miss a log, fill it in later with the earlier date.
bad.why: Backdating makes a false record. A late entry should show its real date.

lines.text: Send requests for personal records to the privacy office.
lines.fine: Sends requests to the people who decide what can be released.

lines.text: Keep required notices posted where employees can see them.
lines.fine: Makes sure everyone can read the rule.

review.notes: Every rule is stated as what this workplace's compliance guide says. No statute is cited or implied. Tiers: safety, then certificate, then record accuracy, then privacy route, then notices.
